transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for taking the time to see me, I really appreciate it. Um... I hope I'm not wasting your time. 

It's just... well, some folks said I should come talk to you because my talking gets a little... mixed up sometimes. It's nothing too terrible, I promise! It's just, I'll try to explain something, like about the keys for my work, and then... then the jail, and the prayer rug, and then chess pieces... and people tell me they just can't follow what I'm saying. 

I don't mean to be confusing, and I try real hard to be clear for them, I really do. Is that... is that something it's okay for me to be here for?

Can you describe what goes through your mind when you're trying to explain something and it starts to get mixed up? Do your thoughts feel connected to each other, or do they jump around in a way that's hard to follow?

That's a really good question, Doctor. I hope I can explain it right for you. Um... to me, they sort of feel connected, but I guess... I guess they do jump around a lot. I'm sorry, I don't want to sound like I'm, you know, losing my mind or anything. It's just... my thoughts, they run so fast sometimes. 

It almost feels like... well, like a whole crowd of folks talking inside my head all at once? I hope that doesn't make me sound too strange. They just jump so quick—like, from worrying about my bills, and then to the jail, and then over to the mosque, and then suddenly I'm thinking about the cleaning chemicals I need for my shift... all before I can even catch hold of just one single thought to say out loud. 

I try really hard to slow them down so I don't bother anyone with it, I really do. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Have you ever had experiences where you believed something strongly that others didn’t seem to understand or agree with, even if you felt it was true at the time?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I really try to get along with everyone at work, I promise. I don't like to cause a fuss. But... there was this one time, and I hope you don't think badly of me for it... 

I just got this feeling, you know? Like the people who run the building had... marked me, somehow. It's silly, I know it sounds silly now. But at the time, I felt like they were using the hallway lights—like, flickering them in a certain way—and giving each other these little looks just to warn each other when I was coming down the hall with my mop cart. 

I actually told my supervisor about it, because I wanted to make sure I wasn't doing anything wrong to upset them. He was real nice about it, he even showed me the security camera footage to prove there was nothing going on. And I know I should have just let it go then, but... I still just felt so sure about it in my gut, even after he showed me. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound difficult to work with. I really do try to do a good job and not bother anyone. Is it... is it normal to get a little worked up like that sometimes?
Do you often feel like people are watching you, talking about you, or acting in certain ways specifically because of something related to you, even if there’s no clear reason for it?

Um... well, I guess that sort of ties into what I was just saying about the hallway lights. I hope it's okay that I brought that up again. I just... I really don't want you to think I'm paranoid or anything like that. I'm usually very easygoing, I promise.

But yes, I suppose I do get those feelings sometimes. Like with the building managers... even after my supervisor was so kind and took the time to show me the camera footage, and I could see with my own eyes there was nothing there... I just couldn't shake it. I still felt so sure, deep down, that they had marked me somehow. That the flickering lights and those little glances they gave each other were all about me. 

I know it doesn't make much sense, and I feel a bit embarrassed even admitting it to you now. I really try not to let those thoughts bother anyone else. Do you... do you think less of me for having those kinds of thoughts, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
When you're speaking, do you find that your sentences themselves stay on track, or do they sometimes become hard to follow even within a single sentence?

Well, um... I guess that's sort of why I'm here, actually. I hope I'm not being too much trouble by saying this. But yes, sometimes, even in just one sentence... things get a little jumbled up. 

I try my best to speak clearly, I really do. I don't want to confuse anybody. But sometimes I'll start trying to explain something simple, like about my keys for work... and then suddenly I'm talking about the jail, and then the prayer rug at the mosque, and then... I don't know, chess pieces? All in the same breath. 

People tell me they can't follow what I'm saying when I get like that. It makes me feel terrible, because I really want to be helpful and easy to understand. I'm sorry, does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too... too mixed up right now. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you ever seen, heard, or sensed things that others around you don’t seem to notice, even when you were sure they were real at the time?

Oh, um... well... I guess I should be honest with you, even if it's a little hard to talk about. I really don't want you to think I'm crazy or anything, Doctor. I know how it sounds. I try to just keep my head down and do my job, but... 

Sometimes, yes. I... I hear things. It's usually when I'm working, like near the air vents or when I'm putting my things away in the mop closet. It's a man's voice. He'll just say my name, or... or sometimes he tells me that I've ruined everything. 

It scares me, to be honest, because it sounds so real. Just like you and me talking right now, like he's standing right next to me. I always look around to see if someone is there, but I'm always alone. I try not to let it bother me, and I never complain about it to anyone at work because I don't want to cause any trouble. 

Is it... is it bad that I hear that? I really hope you don't think I'm making it up or being difficult. I'm just trying to answer your questions the best I can. Am I doing okay?
Are there times when you believe something very strongly, even when others tell you it isn’t true or show you proof that it isn’t?

Um... well, I know I mentioned this earlier, and I hope it's alright to bring it up again. I really don't want to sound like a broken record or make you think I'm just obsessing over things. I try to be very reasonable, I really do. 

But... yes, I guess that happens. Like with the hallway lights at work. My supervisor, who is a very nice person, actually sat down with me and showed me the security camera footage. And I looked at it, I really did, and I could see there was nothing there. 

But even with that proof right in front of me... I just couldn't let it go. Deep down, I still felt this absolute certainty that the building managers had marked me. That the flickering lights and those tiny little looks they gave each other were a warning about me. 

I know it sounds silly now, and I'm really embarrassed to admit that I couldn't just accept what the camera showed. I promise I don't argue with people about it or cause a fuss. I try to keep it to myself so I don't bother anyone. Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need.

Have you ever had beliefs that felt completely true to you, even if they involved things like people sending you secret messages, plotting against you, or something else that others might find hard to believe?

Oh, um... well, yes, Doctor. I think... I think that's exactly what I was just trying to explain, actually. I hope it's okay that I kind of jumped ahead a little bit just now. I didn't mean to talk out of turn. 

But yes, when you say secret messages and plotting... that's exactly what it was with the building managers. Like I was saying, even after my supervisor was so nice to show me the camera footage and prove nothing was there... I still just felt so sure they had marked me. The way those hallway lights flickered, and those... those little looks they would give each other when I walked by with my mop cart... it felt exactly like they were sending secret warnings about me. 

I know it sounds really bad when I say it out loud, like I'm paranoid or something. I promise I don't let it stop me from doing a good job, and I never confront anybody about it. I just keep my head down. I don't want to be a bother to anyone at work. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you meant? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way. Am I doing alright?
Have you ever felt like things in your environment—like TV shows, music, or everyday events—were sending you messages or had special meanings just for you?

Um, well... I guess I might be repeating myself again, and I'm really sorry if I'm not giving you the answers you're looking for. I just want to make sure I'm doing this right. 

But, um... yes, I think that's sort of what I meant about the hallway lights. I don't really watch much TV or listen to the radio, but... everyday events, like you said... that's exactly how it felt with the lights. When they flickered, it didn't just feel like a broken bulb. It felt like... like a message. Like a special meaning just for me, saying that the building people had marked me. And the way they looked at each other... it all felt like a warning. 

Even when my supervisor was so patient and showed me the camera footage, and I could see there was nothing there... I still just couldn't shake that feeling that the lights meant something special about me. 

I know it sounds so silly, and I really hope you don't think I'm just making things up or trying to be difficult. I promise I try to ignore it and just do my work. Does that... does that answer your question, Doctor? Am I being helpful?
Have you ever felt like certain events, actions, or objects in your environment were specifically directed at you or had a special personal meaning that others didn't understand?

Oh dear... I'm so sorry, Doctor. I feel like I'm frustrating you because I keep giving you the exact same answer, and you have to keep asking me. I really don't mean to be difficult or slow to understand... I hope you're not upset with me. 

But, um... yes, sir. It's just like I was saying about the hallway lights and those little looks the building people gave each other. To my supervisor, when she looked at the camera, it was just a regular hallway and normal people. She didn't understand it at all. But to me... it had that special meaning. I just felt so sure they had marked me and were using those things to warn each other about me. 

I'm really sorry I don't have a different example to give you... I just want to be as honest as I can so I don't mess up your evaluation. Is it okay that I keep bringing up the same thing? Am I doing this right?

I just felt so sure they had marked me and were using those things to warn each other about me. 

I'm really sorry I don't have a different example to give you... I just want to be as honest as I can so I don't mess up your evaluation. Is it okay that I keep bringing up the same thing? Am I doing this right?

Although schizoaffective disorder (F25.1) was considered due to the presence of hallucinations and delusions, there was no clear evidence of a major mood episode occurring concurrently with the psychotic symptoms, which is required for that diagnosis.
